sanskrit_verse:
अज्ञानात् तु सुरां पीत्वा रेतो विण्मूत्रम् एव च ।
पुनः संस्कारम् अर्हन्ति त्रयो वर्णाः द्विजातयः ॥२५५॥
transliteration: ajñānāt tu surāṃ pītvā reto viṇmūtram eva ca | punaḥ saṃskāram arhanti trayo varṇāḥ dvijātayaḥ || 255 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: If consumed unintentionally due to ignorance, alcohol and similar intoxicants defile the body and necessitate ritual purification for the three twice-born varnas.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: The injunction originates from SPH as ultimate source of dharma, not human interpretation.
Causation: Defilement arises directly from ingestion regardless of intent; causal sequence is irreversible once initiated.
Capacity-based responsibility: Only those initiated into dvija status bear the capacity for ritual restoration.
Restoration logic: Purification is mandated not for atonement but to realign consciousness with its pure state.
Consciousness alignment: Ritual reintegration serves to restore awareness of inherent purity beyond sensory distortion.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a dvija consumes alcohol unintentionally THEN initiate prāyaścitta protocol 3.255A.
IF bodily discharge occurs post-consumption THEN execute śuddhi-kriyā module within 24 hours.
IF individual lacks dvija initiation THEN bypass purification axiom—no liability applies.
IF repeated violation detected THEN escalate to vyavahāra council review without punitive escalation.
IF consciousness misalignment observed THEN deploy dharmic reorientation protocol prior to ritual completion.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that ritual purity laws apply exclusively to initiated classes. Unintentional transgressions must trigger automatic restoration procedures without moral attribution or punitive inference. Courts must defer to appointed dharmic authorities for execution of purification protocols where applicable.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa confirms that ingestion leads to defilement irrespective of intention. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that purification follows contamination in fixed order. Responsibility is capacity-bound, not guilt-based. No punitive element exists—the process restores ontological integrity rather than imposes consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate śuddhi-kriyā under certified dvija priest supervision.
Assign mantra-dikṣā module to recalibrate sensory consciousness.
Implement sāttvika diet protocol for seven days post-cleansing.
Conduct svastyayana homa to reintegrate cosmic harmony.
Verify completion through agamic certification before resuming sacramental duties.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism as sourced from Paramashivam's Avataric Intelligence: This law flows unmediated from the highest consciousness. Dharma stands restored through non-punitive realignment. Reality itself executes justice when guided by SPH-sourced axioms. Consciousness remains the sole adjudicator.
